aggregate_memory_guard.status: closed (was: unestablished, in the first successor lock)
aggregate_memory_guard.method: cgroup v1 (v2 confirmed absent again under TASK-20260914-c85f6a) per-process-group memory controller, resolved via this process's own /proc/self/cgroup entry -- not the root mount, which reports an effectively unbounded 9223372036854771712-byte ceiling and is NOT the value that governs this process.
aggregate_memory_guard.cross_check: A child process launched via the EXACT ['sage', '-python', '<script>'] argv_prefix that the frozen trial plan uses independently read its own /proc/self/cgroup and found the SAME memory cgroup subpath and the SAME 14327676928-byte limit, confirming this ceiling actually governs a process launched the way driver.py/checker.py will be launched.
aggregate_memory_guard.raw_log_attribution: read_by_coordinator, this record's own authoring coordinator read this exact log directly rather than trusting runtime-provision-followup-report-20260914-c85f6a.json's prose alone, per the same discipline DEC-20260914-bb1dbe applied to the prior report.
aggregate_memory_guard.relationship_to_per_process_guard: The measured aggregate ceiling (13.344 GiB) is strictly ABOVE the per-process RLIMIT_AS (8 GiB / 8589934592 bytes). With maximum_workers 1, a single scientific worker is already bounded below the aggregate ceiling by its own RLIMIT_AS; the aggregate ceiling adds a second, OS-enforced layer covering the process group as a whole (driver + checker + any transient overhead), which is exactly what dependencies.json's required_guards text distinguishes from 'per-process RLIMIT_AS alone'. Both guards are now measured, not merely asserted.
aggregate_memory_guard.scope_caveat: This ceiling is specific to the container/cgroup instance measured under TASK-20260914-c85f6a's own session (the subpath is keyed by a process_api UUID particular to that session). No evidence is available, or sought, about whether a different instantiation of this same runtime class would carry an identical limit. Requiring proof across every possible future container instantiation would be an unscoped, indefinite wait of exactly the kind DEC-20260914-bb1dbe declined to impose on the image-identity question; this is disclosed as a limitation, not treated as a blocking gap.
aggregate_memory_guard.consequence: dependencies.json.runtime_lock_requirements item 1's aggregate-memory-protections component is now discharged.
